newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Seoul shares lose heavily on tycoon sentencing.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares lose heavily on tycoon sentencing.

text.p: The sentencing of nine South Korean business tycoons added to the country's economic worries on Monday and sent Seoul shares diving to a 33-month-low.
Most other Asian markets declined amid trade made sluggish by holidays for the London and Hong Kong markets.
Seoul's composite stock index fell 15.24 points, or 1.95 percent, to 766.89, the lowest close since November 4, 1993, when it ended at 766.55.
"The entire market is depressed right now because of the economic slow-down. The sentencing of the business leaders is making the sentiment worse," said a Hanyang Securities broker.
The head of Samsung, Lee Kun-hee, was sentenced to a two-year prison term suspended for three years. Daewoo's Kim Woo-choong was sentenced to two years in jail.
The tycoons were sentenced for giving bribes to former South Korean president, Roh Tae-woo, who succeeded Chun Doo Hwan.
The same court also sentenced Chun to death on charges of treason and corruption. Roh was sentenced to 22-1/2 years in prison for playing a supporting role.
Yonhap news agency quoted unnamed finance ministry officials as saying they were concerned overseas investors would be scared away by the sentencing.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei 225 stock average lost 1.63 percent on bouts of futures-linked selling.
"The end of the month is approaching and important economic indicators are due out this week, keeping participants away," said Masaaki Higashida, strategist at Nomura Securities.
The Nikkei tumbled 345.06 points to close at 20,883.74.
In Singapore, shares finished sharply lower in thin trading as support shifted from second liners to Malaysian over-the-counter stocks.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index lost 21.49 points, or 0.99 percent, to 2,160.03.
Thai stocks declined by 1.02 percent after investors took profits and foreign interest remained slack due to a holiday in Hong Kong, brokers said.
The SET index ended 11.29 points lower at 1,095.44.
"The market lacked positive news while investors continued worrying about local economic and political problems," said Virat Tippanontakul of First Asia Securities.
Manila's stock market ended a three-day winning streak as investors cashed in on their gains and set aside money for initial public offerings, traders said.
The main index fell 16.16 points, or 0.50 percent, to 3,210.30 points after Friday's 38.68-point advance.
Taiwan shares closed slightly higher amid investor caution over Taiwan's economic policy towards China, brokers said.
The index ended up 9.92 points or 0.16 percent at 6,200.48.
Jakarta share prices closed higher despite weak regional markets following active trade in selected second-liners and blue chips, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 3.53 points, or 0.64 percent, to close at 552.74 points. Losers led gainers by 61 to 37, with 43 counters unchanged.
The Australian share market ended 0.47 percent lower as weakness in a bruised and battered bond market flowed through to equities.
The All Ordinaries index was down 10.8 points at 2,282.1.
In Tokyo, the dollar was little changed in late dealings from closing levels on Friday on New York, with movements stuck to narrow ranges amid a dearth of fresh factors, dealers said.
At 630 GMT, the dollar traded at 108.05/15 yen and at 1.4787/94 marks.
Asian crude oil prices were flat to slightly lower in a market deprived of direction from London.
In Tokyo, spot gold was quoted at $388.20/50 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $388.00/388.50 in New York on Friday.
